questions.stem: On workstation ws-1996, which sits at 192.0.2.247, consider how a packet network works. Which of the following best explains TCP goodput estimation?
questions.subject: COMPUTER_NETWORKS

questions.explanation: If a sender can have W bytes outstanding and each round trip takes R seconds, then it can deliver about W over R bytes per second, assuming no loss. Increasing the window or reducing delay raises goodput; increasing delay lowers it. Loss and congestion control can reduce the effective window below the advertised one, so the ratio is an upper estimate rather than a guarantee. The concrete addresses in the case do not change the rule.
questions.hint: Check the units of bytes divided by seconds.
